title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents drawn deterministically from a preregistered generator; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate; model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; one initial generation per intent shared across baseline and guarded conditions; guarded pipeline permitted ≤1 repair call. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We highlight a methodological lesson: preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states if applied directly [1]–[3]. A commonly proposed defense is a generate→verify→repair architecture in which an LLM produces a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and an automated repair (or human gate) corrects violations before execution [4], [5]. Security analyses of agentic LLM pipelines further motivate deterministic gating because unchecked textual claims can become harmful actions in multi-tool workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen before any model outputs were observed.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-backed outcomes showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (+0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A focused methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials include baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly specify generation semantics because semantics materially change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work:
Related literature spans intent-translation evaluations, verifier-guided repair systems, formal verifier tooling, and agentic/tool-augmented safety analyses. Intent-translation and intent-driven configuration work report that free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants, and published benchmarks and surveys show modest semantic-correctness rates on heterogeneous task banks [1], [2].

A growing body of work integrates deterministic verification into generation workflows and reports improved practical correctness, but reported gains depend strongly on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, and repair budget (e.g., TerraFormer in IaC) [2], [7]. Independent benchmark efforts for LLM-driven configuration repair likewise show that generate→verify→repair pipelines can improve downstream validity, yet effect sizes vary with sampling and repair regimes [3].

Formal-verification tools such as NetKAT/KATch and related symbolic engines provide concrete oracles for reachability, isolation, and policy checks and are commonly proposed as gating layers for LLM-generated configurations [5]. Security studies demonstrate that unguarded multi-tool agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions and are vulnerable to prompt-injection; these results motivate auditable verifier gating [6]. Our study operationalizes these ideas under a strict preregistered, paired design and explicit execution semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 with a frozen analysis plan executed before any model outputs were observed. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents produced deterministically by the preregistered generator; deterministic inclusion/exclusion rules (ambiguity detector, verifier-coverage checks); and a preregistered power target to detect an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement (~80% power) under conservative discordant-pair assumptions.

Execution semantics and explicit mapping to preregistration labels. A central design decision was execution-semantic enforcement of shared_initial_candidate: for each intent the adapter produced exactly one initial model generation and that identical sampled candidate was used in the paired evaluation of both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline was permitted at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. To remove any ambiguity between preregistration labels and the executed contrasts, we state explicitly: preregistration conceptualized three conditions (A: baseline free-text, B: constrained/template prompting, C: constrained + verifier-feedback). Under the adapter enforcement for this run the primary confirmatory contrast executed and archived is C vs A under shared_initial_candidate semantics (i.e., marginal effect of applying at most one repair to the identical initial sample). The constrained-only condition B was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run and therefore no B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts (as independent-condition comparisons) are reported in the archived analysis. All subsequent analytic claims are restricted to the executed C vs A paired comparison under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Model, sampling, validator, and task generator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses); recorded configuration declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, independent API sessions may produce nondeterministic outputs; this nondeterminism was anticipated and accounted for by the preregistration via execution semantics and paired design. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned binary pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration and diagnostics. Confirmatory tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access, VLAN/MTU sequences, and uplink switchover). Parser/unit-tests that map textual outputs to verifier inputs were run before batch execution and passed as preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. No contamination flags or preregistered-unit-test failures occurred.

Primary numerical outcomes. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These figures are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150) and converted one initially invalid baseline candidate into a valid guarded outcome. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). The single discordant pair corresponds to pair-000069 in the archived raw results; representative validator traces for that pair and others are preserved in the execution bundle for audit.

Preregistered power assumption invalidation. The preregistered power calculation targeted a detectable absolute improvement of +15 percentage points; the observed baseline_success_rate ≈99.33% produced a ceiling effect that invalidated that detectable-effect assumption and left very little discordant-pair information for inference. No post-preregistration analytic changes were made: the reported confirmatory test follows the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 and uses the preregistered handling of incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary).
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and methodological lesson. The near-ceiling baseline undermined our ability to detect the preregistered target effect. We therefore recommend that preregistered NetOps trials include a short baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks sampled from the planned generator and prompt style) to estimate baseline competence and discordant-pair proportions prior to selecting confirmatory N or task difficulty.

Semantics, sampling, and estimand trade-offs. Shared_initial_candidate semantics make the guarded−baseline contrast a marginal-repair estimand: it isolates the effect of applying up to one repair to the identical initial sample. Alternative semantics (independent per-condition sampling, multi-draw ensembles, or larger repair budgets) answer different operational questions and typically require more model calls; practitioners should select semantics that match deployment constraints and account for model-call cost in experimental design.

Operational affordances beyond pass/fail. Even when marginal pass-rate gains are small, guarded pipelines generate verifier diagnostics (violation codes, normalized configurations, counterexamples) that improve operational observability, accelerate triage, and support auditable change records. These qualitative benefits warrant evaluation in cost–benefit experiments that vary repair budgets, sampling semantics, and latency constraints.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audits mitigated cross-condition leakage; parser/unit-tests reduced mapping failures. Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to other models, vendor CLIs, or large heterogeneous WANs. Security: adversarial prompt-injection was not evaluated here and remains an independent concern.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
